persona: First-time RILL user and beginner music producer interested in a small electronic dance groove; independent mouse-only simulated participant, not a human study.

findings.observation: The empty-lane Double-click for MIDI prompt led directly to the Device library and Assign instrument created a lane with Rill Lab Sine and an empty pattern.
Pencil drags created labelled notes, and drawing beyond the initial one-bar pattern automatically extended it to four bars.
I consulted Tool help to learn that Duplicate requires clicking a clip after choosing the tool. It then copied both selected lanes together successfully.
Cutting near the ruler's 30-second label with 1/16 snapping produced 30.134 seconds. Bar snapping and repeated final-edge gestures achieved 30.000; precise narrow-edge targeting required care.
A drag at the loop-strip end did not visibly extend the loop. Range > Loop arrangement solved the task clearly.
Rename project exposed a visible on-screen keyboard, enabling mouse-only entry of Neon Pocket. Save and export pickers reused this name.
During playback, transport position advanced and the drum, MIDI, and master meters displayed activity. No capture was auditioned.
The native save picker initially rendered as a black rectangle before its controls appeared. WAV export required a noticeable wait but displayed elapsed progress and then a success message.
WAV export clearly stated the arrangement duration and format. Both WAV and MIDI exports ended with explicit Exported messages.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: Visible prompts, note drawing, and File commands supported completing the task; exact trimming needed retries.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: Polished dark teal styling, readable controls, and clear waveforms.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Drawing and duplication responded promptly; file pickers and WAV rendering introduced waits with eventual feedback.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Some uncertainty about tool activation, loop-edge dragging, and note colors, but help and menus resolved the important tasks. Higher values mean more confusing.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: All core features needed for this small audio-and-MIDI piece were available. Advanced production and other instruments were outside the session.

outcome.status: Completed through visible mouse UI; awaiting coordinator's independent file verification.
outcome.composition: Fourteen bars: supplied drum audio repeated and trimmed, plus a hand-drawn four-bar MIDI phrase repeated three times with a final two-bar section. Pitches include C4, D4, E4, F4, G4, and A4.
outcome.instrument: Rill Lab Sine VST3 assigned through Device library; track name remained New instrument.
outcome.project_save_evidence: Accepted Neon Pocket.rill in the native session-2 save picker; unsaved-change indicator disappeared.
outcome.wav_export_evidence: Exported Neon Pocket.wav success message; arrangement 0:30, 48 kHz stereo 32-bit float, effect tails unchecked.

limitations: Simulated beginner session, not a human participant study.
Only the supplied technical-control instructions, session screenshots, and visible UI were inspected; no source code, app data, or peer study records were read.
All app interaction used the provided mouse driver; no keyboard events, shortcuts, state APIs, or composition-file edits.
Playback was assessed visually through transport and meters; no audio capture was auditioned, and audible sound quality is unassessed.
Artifact contents and exact exported durations were not read directly and require independent verification.
Software graphics and timer-paced virtual audio with 60 ms buffering are laboratory conditions; speed and latency findings do not characterize physical hardware.
Only the installed Rill Lab Sine native VST3 instrument was exercised; findings do not establish behavior of other plug-ins.
